1988-04.title: TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery
1988-04.disposition_detail: Complaint partially sustained; Presbytery's instruction to transfer three ruling elders annulled; constitutional safeguards directed
1988-04.summary: Philadelphia Presbytery ordered Christ Church, Oreland’s Session to transfer three ruling elders while their judicial cases were on appeal. The General Assembly adopted its special Judicial Commission’s judgment rejecting the improper-debate specification for insufficient documentation but sustaining the constitutional challenge: BCO 12-5 and the separation of church-court powers reserve membership control to the Session, which correctly withheld transfer during pending judicial process. The judgment annulled Presbytery’s instruction and imposed three-year constitutional-inquiry safeguards, plus Digest purchase and officer review.

1988-06.title: TE John T. DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia Presbytery
1988-06.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained and Presbytery's action annulled; trials de novo produced mixed guilty and not-guilty verdicts and censures
1988-06.summary: A complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of proceedings that cleared teaching and ruling elders without properly trying serious public accusations arising from Christ Church’s division. All three specifications were sustained because plea bargaining, dropped charges, and failure to hear necessary witnesses left the accusations unresolved. Presbytery’s action was annulled and de novo trials produced mixed convictions and acquittals. Harold Burkhart received six months’ suspension, Douglas McCready an admonition, and six former ruling elders three-month suspensions. The decision stressed taking such conflicts to Presbytery or judicial process rather than the congregation.

2018-02.title: Anna Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
2018-02.disposition_detail: BCO 40-5 filing found out of order because Chapter 40 matters reach the SJC only upon General Assembly referral
2018-02.summary: After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session's alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews.

2019-04.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; Presbytery's approval annulled; matter returned to the PJC, which may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32
2019-04.summary: An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC blended a BCO 32 case of process with a BCO 38-1 case without process. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC. Because he admitted only some indicted charges, his negotiated confession could not satisfy BCO 38-1 and the conversion prejudiced his rights. The PJC may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32; the ruling does not decide whether conversion is ever permissible.

2021-07.title: RE J. Lance Acree v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
2021-07.disposition_detail: Complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because Acree lacked standing under BCO 43-1
2021-07.summary: RE Acree attempted to complain directly to Tennessee Valley Presbytery about action taken at a meeting where he was not a commissioner. The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 43-1 gave him no standing to complain against that action. It added that Presbytery should itself have declined to adjudicate the complaint.

1983-06.disposition_detail: Items 2 and part of 5 sustained; Items 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 not sustained
1983-06.summary: Members of New Life Presbyterian Church challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's commission over its handling of membership dismissals and compliance with earlier Assembly directions. The General Assembly commission held that the presbytery commission exceeded BCO 57-5 membership requirements and sustained a related item in part, but did not sustain the remaining claims, including that the commission had failed to act or caused the entire conflict.

1983-10.disposition_detail: Item 4 sustained in part; Items 1, 2, 3, and 5 not sustained
1983-10.summary: David Lockwood Jr. and Evan Holyfield challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's commission for allegedly failing to act and mishandling discipline and reconciliation at New Life Presbyterian Church. The General Assembly commission rejected the failure-to-act claims, citing twenty-three meetings, and found that the complainants had not followed the reconciliation plan; it nevertheless sustained one overlapping membership-discipline item in part by reference to its ruling in Case 6.

1990-02.disposition_detail: Appeal abandoned under BCO 43-7; North Texas Presbytery affirmed
1990-02.summary: First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett appealed after North Texas Presbytery reversed the Session's indefinite suspension of two members who had begun attending other churches. The SJC did not reach the asserted procedural errors because the Session advised that it would start over and would not pursue the appeal. Under BCO 43-7, the appeal was abandoned and Presbytery's judgment was affirmed.

1988-02.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in part and remanded; report of the Commission to Adjudicate Case 2 adopted
1988-02.summary: Fox challenged a Session’s acceptance of his resignation while censured, refusal to restore him, denial of relevant records, and allegedly uneven discipline in his marital dispute. The Assembly adopted the commission’s judgment sustaining the first, third, and fourth complaints: he remained a member, so his removal and nonrestoration were improper and he was entitled to relevant records. Those matters were remanded for rectification. The uneven-discipline claim was neither sustained nor denied because the evidence was insufficient; it too was remanded for investigation and necessary action.

1980-04.disposition_detail: Both counts sustained (10-5 and 15-0); matter remanded for corrective action
1980-04.summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery's sustaining of ordination trials for a candidate who affirmed continuing revelation through interpreted tongues and its approval of a campus-ministry call lacking required terms. The Assembly sustained both counts, holding that the examination left the candidate's views unclarified and failed adequately to protect the Standards' teaching on the finality and sufficiency of Scripture; Presbytery conceded the call's omission. It remanded the matter to obtain a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examine the candidate.

1990-01.title: First Presbyterian Church of Rowlett, Texas v. North Texas Presbytery
1990-01.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained and denied; North Texas Presbytery affirmed
1990-01.summary: A church challenged North Texas Presbytery’s approval of Rev. C. Don Darling, who disclosed that he could not conscientiously accept or conduct remarriage after divorce. The Standing Judicial Commission did not sustain and denied the complaint, affirming Presbytery. Ministerial acceptance ordinarily rests within a presbytery’s jurisdiction, and Darling’s exception neither concerned a fundamental of the doctrinal system nor struck at the vitals of religion or threatened much injury. Overriding Presbytery would therefore improperly impair liberty of conscience.

1992-10.title: Mr. and Mrs. Matthew Bernard v. Ascension Presbytery
1992-10.summary: The Bernards appealed directly to the General Assembly from their excommunication by a Presbytery commission acting as the congregation’s Session. The SJC ruled the appeal administratively out of order because an appeal must first go to the next higher court—Ascension Presbytery—not to the court of original jurisdiction. It did not decide whether the excommunication was proper; that issue remained for Presbytery to hear.

1997-05.disposition_detail: Assembly rejected the minority report, adopted the majority report, and denied the complaint
1997-05.summary: Mt. Carmel Session challenged New Jersey Presbytery's creation-days resolution, arguing that the Westminster Standards require six consecutive twenty-four-hour days. The SJC majority concluded that Presbytery could resolve the doctrinal question under BCO 11-4 and that prior Assembly actions permitted latitude on the length of the creation days. The General Assembly rejected the minority report, adopted the majority report, and denied the complaint.

1999-01.disposition_detail: Request administratively out of order; no merits decision
1999-01.summary: Three presbyteries asked the General Assembly under BCO 34-1 to assume original jurisdiction over a minister alleged to have allowed women to preach from a church pulpit. The SJC held the requests administratively out of order and did not reach the allegation’s merits. Worship was the Session’s responsibility, so the minister could not be held liable for actions assigned to it; moreover, Tennessee Valley Presbytery had acted on the allegations, defeating BCO 34-1’s refusal-to-act prerequisite. No further proceedings were ordered.

2001-37.title: Moo S. Lim et al. v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-37.summary: The SJC ruled the complaint against Korean Capital Presbytery administratively out of order. Because the complainants had not first filed the matter with, and obtained action from, the session as required by BCO 33-1, it was not properly before either Presbytery or the SJC. The ruling did not address the complaint’s merits.

2002-04.title: Judicial Reference from Evangel Presbytery for Adjudication
2002-04.disposition_detail: Judicial reference not acceded to by the SJC
2002-04.summary: Evangel Presbytery asked the SJC to accept and adjudicate a judicial reference. The SJC did not accede to the request. The published report gives no reason for declining the reference and no judgment on the underlying matter.

2002-11.disposition_detail: One complaint issue sustained, remaining issues denied, and underlying complaint remanded
2002-11.summary: Abshire challenged Presbytery’s commission for its appointment, scope, exhortation, summary disposition of two elders’ complaint, and other actions. The SJC sustained only the challenge to deciding the elders’ complaint without BCO 43 procedures and remanded that complaint. It denied the other issues: the commission could conduct the required investigation, the scope objection was untimely, and its exhortation and report were pastoral rather than formal discipline. A separate sixth issue remained before Presbytery and was not decided.

2004-04.summary: The SJC held Jerguson’s appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 because Western Carolina Presbytery was rehearing the case. The matter therefore was not ready for higher-court review. The decision did not reach the merits or dismiss the underlying Presbytery proceedings.

2007-02.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in part; judgment and censure vacated
2007-02.summary: Malone challenged Presbytery’s approval of a commission’s judgment and indefinite suspension imposed without process. The SJC sustained the complaint in part and vacated the judgment and censure: the commission had authority only to investigate, and Malone’s general acknowledgments neither confessed specific charges nor showed intent to waive process under BCO 38-1. Presbytery could begin anew under proper procedures. The SJC rejected Malone’s claim that suggested steps evidencing repentance improperly bound him, treating them as noncompulsory pastoral advice.

2007-15.disposition_detail: Complaint found out of order; no merits decision
2007-15.summary: TE Sang Chul Choi’s complaint against Korean Central Presbytery was found out of order. The sparse published record does not identify the challenged presbytery action, specify an administrative or judicial subtype, explain the ruling, or resolve the merits.

2008-04.disposition_detail: Complaint found out of order; no merits decision
2008-04.summary: The recorded disposition found Acree’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery out of order. The sparse record does not identify the challenged presbytery action, give a reason for the ruling, or designate it as administratively or judicially out of order. No merits determination or substantive relief appears.

2008-05.disposition_detail: Complaint found out of order; no merits decision
2008-05.summary: The published Assembly record lists Acree’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery as out of order. It provides no description of the challenged action, rationale, or merits determination. Although the source header labels the disposition “Withdrawn,” the operative record says that a different case, 2008-02, was withdrawn.

2008-09.title: Session of Red Mountain Presbyterian Church v. Evangel Presbytery
2008-09.disposition_detail: All four elements sustained; Presbytery's action reversed
2008-09.summary: Red Mountain Session challenged Presbytery’s ruling that it had inadequately addressed a member’s demand to declare his wife’s divorce unbiblical, and Presbytery’s resulting declaration and Matthew 18 instruction. The SJC sustained all four issues and reversed Presbytery. It held Session’s context-sensitive ruling disclosed no clear error, use of BCO 31-2 was reasonable, Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by allowing its commission to revise a report after floor discussion, and Presbytery judged the wife without due process. The SJC expressly did not decide whether biblical divorce grounds existed.

2008-11.summary: Presbytery empowered a commission both to assume original jurisdiction over matters involving church members and to receive a Session's reference concerning a membership transfer. The SJC vacated the original-jurisdiction mandate because Presbytery had neither found that the Session refused to act nor required the commission to make that finding before proceeding. The authority to receive the reference remained intact; requests from other Sessions alone did not satisfy BCO 33-1.

2008-13.disposition_detail: Complaint moot in light of the decision in Case 2008-11
2008-13.summary: Meyerhoff challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s called meeting to receive, discuss, and entertain questions about an original-jurisdiction commission’s initial report. Without deciding whether those actions were procedurally erroneous, the SJC held the complaint moot in view of its judgment in Case 2008-11. It directed Presbytery to note the mootness ruling in the minutes of the August 16, 2008 meeting.

2010-05.title: Dale Cutler v. Platte Valley Presbytery
2010-05.summary: Dale Cutler filed a complaint against Platte Valley Presbytery. The SJC found it administratively out of order, but the sparse report does not identify the challenged action, explain the procedural defect, or provide further relief. It therefore supports no conclusion about the complaint's merits.

2010-06.title: Peter Yuan v. South Coast Presbytery
2010-06.summary: Peter Yuan appealed to the SJC regarding alleged heresy by Samuel Ling. The Commission found Case 2010-06 administratively out of order. This brief status report supplies no reason for that ruling and identifies no further relief or proceedings.

2011-08.summary: Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.

2011-17.disposition_detail: Part of one allegation sustained; four allegations not sustained; censure left intact
2011-17.summary: Ministers challenged Jeremy Smith's excommunication, but not his deposition. The SJC rejected four allegations and most of the fifth, holding among other things that two ignored citations are only one possible form of contumacy. It sustained the complaint solely because Presbytery wrongly treated Smith's absence as a refusal to appear: a committee email was not a citation by Presbytery. The SJC reversed that finding but did not annul the excommunication, leaving Presbytery to consider whether modification was necessary.

2013-03.summary: Marshall complained that Pacific Presbytery wrongly refused to dismiss a judicial case despite alleged procedural irregularities in the indictment and process. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order: objections arising in a judicial case were to be preserved for appeal under BCO 32-14 and 42-3, and Marshall’s pending appeal independently barred a complaint under BCO 43-1. It granted no complaint relief. Separate opinions disputed the first rationale but agreed that the pending appeal barred the complaint.

2016-05.disposition_detail: Complaint partially sustained; challenged action annulled
2016-05.summary: A complaint challenged Presbytery’s institution of two charges against a teaching elder and related pretrial actions. The SJC annulled the household-management charge because process began fifteen months after the alleged offense and the record showed no recently flagrant, newly evident, or continuing offense under BCO 32-20. It also held that declaring the elder not in good standing removed rights without process, but left his properly imposed suspension effective. It rejected objections to discussion, questioning, and the timely submission charge, which could proceed without any determination of guilt.

2017-05.title: BCO 40-5 Report of TE James Bachmann
2017-05.summary: The SJC docket records TE James Bachmann's BCO 40-5 report as out of order. The published record does not identify the procedural defect, describe the underlying allegations, or decide whether an important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceeding occurred.

2019-01.disposition_detail: Complaint partially sustained; further proceedings moot
2019-01.summary: Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.

2020-12.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; all stated issues answered no
2020-12.summary: Ryan Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its refusal to commence process against Greg Johnson on four allegations concerning same-sex attraction as sin, identity in Christ, sanctification, and fitness for office. The SJC denied the complaint in full. It found no clear procedural error and held that Johnson’s explanations and clarifications made Presbytery’s non-indictment judgments reasonable. No trial was ordered. The ruling neither adjudged Johnson guilty nor endorsed every statement or broader constitutional position concerning same-sex attraction.

2022-05.disposition_detail: Complaint out of order and moot
2022-05.summary: Three Ruling Elders complained of errors in judicial process against them. The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot because the Session had dismissed every charge and ended the process, while the elders had voluntarily resigned and requested dissolution of their calls. Because these events removed the challenged action and settled the underlying dispute, the SJC did not reach the alleged procedural errors.

1976-01.disposition_detail: Complaint found invalid because McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity
1976-01.summary: A session complained that Covenant Presbytery violated PCA standards by approving the summer employment of a divorced and remarried man in a ministerial capacity. The Judicial Commission found the complaint invalid, holding that McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity. It expressly did not decide whether such employment would violate the Constitution. The General Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment, leaving the presbytery's action undisturbed.

1977-03.title: Rev. Thomas Barnes et al. v. Evangel Presbytery
1977-03.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained; written call requirement emphasized and broader question referred to the CJB
1977-03.summary: The Fifth General Assembly approved its Judicial Commission’s refusal to sustain a complaint challenging Presbytery’s approval of Mercer for ordination as an evangelist without a call and for parachurch work outside its bounds. No reason for rejecting the complaint was stated. The ruling nevertheless required Presbytery to have—and itself issue—a written call before implementing the ordination decision, and requested referral of the broader question defining a valid ministerial call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business.

1984-04.disposition_detail: Continued non-compliance and constitutional violation sustained 12-3; contumacy not sustained 1-14; remedial recommendations adopted
1984-04.summary: Ascension Presbytery was challenged for resolving not to comply with prior General Assembly directions concerning an ordination examination. The case was sustained as to continued noncompliance and constitutional violation, but not as to contumacy; remedial recommendations were adopted. The supplied text contains the complaint rather than the operative judgment, so it does not disclose the adjudicative reasoning or the specific remedial measures.

1984-07.disposition_detail: Continued non-compliance sustained 15-0; constitutional violation not sustained 5-8-2; contumacy not sustained 0-13-2; remedial recommendations adopted
1984-07.summary: A Session and other complainants challenged Presbytery’s May 1984 resolution as continued noncompliance with directions from an earlier ordination case. The continued-noncompliance specification was sustained, but allegations of constitutional violation and contumacy were not sustained. Remedial recommendations were adopted, although the supplied excerpt provides neither their terms nor the deciding body’s reasons. The mixed ruling therefore distinguishes noncompliance from the complainants’ more serious characterizations of Presbytery’s conduct.

1997-07.title: Steve Farris v. Central Florida Presbytery
1997-07.disposition_detail: Complaint judicially out of order because the complainant was not a member of a PCA church and lacked standing
1997-07.summary: The Standing Judicial Commission held Steve Farris's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery judicially out of order because Farris was not a member of a PCA church and therefore lacked standing before the Commission. The Commission reached no merits issue and granted no relief; the only stated ground was the complainant's lack of standing. The case illustrates a threshold standing bar for SJC complainants, but the sparse record does not identify the underlying presbytery action complained of.

1999-04.title: Ed Fitzsimmons v. Evangel Presbytery
1999-04.disposition_detail: Appeal administratively out of order because it was not filed with the Stated Clerk within thirty days as required by BCO 42-2
1999-04.summary: The SJC refused to hear Ed Fitzsimmons's appeal from Evangel Presbytery because his appeal was not filed with the General Assembly's Stated Clerk within the 30-day deadline of BCO 42-2. The appeal was declared administratively out of order, and no merits question was decided. The sparse record shows a straightforward application of the filing deadline; it does not disclose the underlying presbytery action or any merits view.

1999-07.title: Jeffrey M. Black v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
1999-07.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained; Eastern Carolina Presbytery did not err on either issue
1999-07.summary: Black challenged Presbytery’s handling of his complaint and its ruling that a licentiate’s non-24-hour creation-day view was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC denied remand because Presbytery had effectively adjudicated the complaint; the separate objection to proceeding without Black was not first filed below and was administratively out of order. It upheld Presbytery’s ruling that not every non-Calendar-Day view constitutes an exception. Because the record did not identify the licentiate’s precise view, the decision did not determine its acceptability or whether it could be taught.

2006-06.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; North Georgia Presbytery did not err in sustaining the Session's instruction against distributing the open letter
2006-06.summary: Members challenged Presbytery’s denial of their complaint against a Session instruction not to circulate an open letter repeating allegations against their pastor. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the instruction in force. It held that liberty of conscience does not eliminate members’ obligation to obey lawful church injunctions. Here the members had sought the Session’s advice, Presbytery had found no strong presumption of chargeable offenses, and renewed circulation would disturb the church’s peace; under those circumstances, the Session acted within its authority.

2006-02.standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
2006-02.summary: In a BCO 40-5 memorial, Central Carolina Presbytery alleged that Louisiana Presbytery had exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite his published views on election, the church, perseverance, assurance, and baptism allegedly contradicting the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the memorial’s gravity and found Presbytery failed to show due diligence, ordering a recorded examination, formal responses, and report. Presbytery later met the procedural directives, but the SJC relied on Case 2007-8’s substantive finding, cited Presbytery under BCO 40-5, and appointed a prosecutor for Case 2007-14.

2007-14.disposition_detail: Specification 1 dismissed after trial; Louisiana Presbytery's guilty plea to Specification 2 accepted and censure of admonition imposed
2007-14.summary: In this BCO 40-5 proceeding over Louisiana Presbytery’s investigation of TE Stephen Wilkins, the SJC dismissed Specification 1 because it could not find that the cited procedures were constitutionally required or that guilt was proved. The dismissal did not erase concerns about undocumented doctrinal findings; those failures were covered by Specification 2. On Presbytery’s guilty plea to that specification, the SJC imposed a public admonition for failing to find a strong presumption of doctrinal guilt and pursue trial. Wilkins’s and his church’s withdrawal made practical amends unavailable.
2007-14.standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings; this was a 40-5/40-6 trial rather than an ordinary appeal.

2010-08.summary: The SJC report lists Case 2010-08, Mr. Michael A. McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery, among cases found judicially out of order. No separate merits opinion was published, and the available report does not identify the challenged action, procedural vehicle, or reasons. The only usable result is the judicial out-of-order classification; no merits determination or relief is stated.

2022-22.disposition_detail: Issue 1 denied; Issue 2 sustained; findings of guilt and censures annulled; matter returned to South Florida Presbytery for constitutionally appropriate proceedings
2022-22.summary: Presbytery investigated a Session's handling of sexual-misconduct allegations and found it guilty of delinquencies without a trial. The SJC upheld Presbytery's authority to receive credible reports and investigate, but annulled the findings of guilt, censures, and corrective mandates because BCO 40-6 required formal process or an admission before censure. It returned the matter for records review, informal resolution, or formal process and declined interim mandates that would assume the disputed allegations were true.

2023-09.disposition_detail: Appeal sustained 21-1; Presbytery's action reversed in whole and prior suspensions restored pending constitutionally adequate process
2023-09.summary: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

2016-14.standard_of_review_detail: Issue 1 applies BCO 39-3.4 to constitutional interpretation; Issue 2 applies BCO 39-3.3 to discretion and judgment.
2016-14.summary: Did a presbytery violate the BCO or clearly err by dissolving a congregation without its consent? The SJC said no and denied the complaint. On the constitutional issue, it held that BCO 13-9.f grants dissolution power and BCO 40-6 does not impose formal process for it. On the discretionary issue, it found no clear error in the record. The denial left dissolution in place and warned that such action still requires sufficient justification and prudent, reviewable procedure.

2019-11.standard_of_review_detail: The adopted opinion applies BCO 39-3.3 to the Session's exercise of discretion and judgment; the dissent argues for BCO 39-3.4 but does not alter the majority holding.
2019-11.summary: A complaint challenging a session's refusal to advance an ordained deacon's nomination for re-election to the diaconate was denied by the SJC. Northwest Georgia Presbytery had adopted its judicial commission's judgment that the session did not err; applying BCO 39-3(3)'s deference to discretionary judgments, the SJC found no clear error, held formal charges were unnecessary and re-election was not guaranteed, and refused to attribute one elder's questionable retaliation rationale to the session. The majority encouraged prompt communication of reasons. A dissent would apply BCO 39-3.4 and sustain.

2020-05.standard_of_review_detail: The adopted opinion resolves the complaint on the constitutional criteria and procedural errors identified, without stating a distinct BCO 39-3 standard of review.
2020-05.summary: Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s approval of six theological judgments concerning teachings at Revoice 18, its rejection of his procedural point of order, and its refusal to debate gay-couple adoption. The SJC sustained only the first issue, particularly as to Judgments 2, 3, and 5: Presbytery improperly imported BCO 34-5’s ministerial-process standard into court review and then inadequately addressed identified errors affecting church peace and purity. It rejected the procedural and adoption claims and remanded for a focused new hearing under BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f).

2023-14.disposition_detail: BCO 40-5 ruling found egregious constitutional error and fully redressed the reported matter, but denied the requested annulment of the installations.
2023-14.standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings; the SJC found egregious constitutional error and addressed the requested relief.
2023-14.summary: Presbytery approved calls and installed three associate pastors after a constitutionally deficient election. The SJC found egregious error, including slate voting, a standing rather than ballot vote, and failure to determine and record the number of voters present under the then-current rule. It nevertheless denied the requested annulment of the installations because PCA judicial proceedings supplied no precedent and the remedy's legitimacy was doubtful. The SJC stayed further proceedings and declared the report concluded.

2022-10.summary: On a BCO 41 reference, the SJC tried a minister on seven charges arising from allegations of sexual misconduct, bullying, dishonesty, a civil defamation suit, contumacy, doctrinal error, and lack of fitness. It found him not guilty on every charge because the prosecution failed to meet its burden, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to good standing. For the lawsuit charge, it rejected a categorical ban on civil suits between Christians and required proof that this suit was sinful.

1991-01.title: Sandra Lovelace v. Northeast Presbytery
1991-01.summary: The SJC found two attempted complaints administratively and judicially out of order. The October 1990 filing did not satisfy BCO 43-2 because the earlier letters it invoked had merely asked questions or communicated concern, rather than first presenting a complaint to Presbytery, and concerned an oral report not made part of Presbytery's record. The January 1991 filing supplied no supporting reasons as BCO 43-3 required and challenged specifications of error that were not themselves acts or decisions of Presbytery.
1991-01.disposition_detail: Both letters found administratively and judicially out of order

1991-03.title: Daniel R. Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
1991-03.summary: On Covenant Presbytery’s mixed BCO 41 reference, the SJC held that ministers Morse and Crenshaw could not resign unilaterally; joining another evangelical church invoked BCO 38-3, requiring their names erased, with notice that they were in good standing and faced no pending charges. Grace Church’s withdrawal required a congregational vote, not notice to Presbytery, so its name also was to be erased. Grace had abandoned its complaints, rendering them moot; the SJC nevertheless opined that recording a protest is insulated from complaint by BCO 45-5.
1991-03.disposition_detail: Complaints abandoned as moot; SJC issued final directions on ministerial and congregational roll status

1991-04.title: Robert D. Hopper v. James River Presbytery
1991-04.summary: The SJC denied Hopper's complaint against James River Presbytery's April 13, 1991 order barring him from teaching or preaching his views on prophecy and tongues. It rejected all five specifications: Scripture did not forbid the order; the 1974 Pastoral Letter did not address presbytery's power to enjoin such teaching; forbearance did not preclude protecting peace and purity; presbytery could restrict preaching short of a heresy finding without binding conscience; and allowing presbyteral discussion while restricting congregational teaching was not inconsistent. The action remained in force.

1991-05.title: Herman Gunter III et al. v. Central Florida Presbytery
1991-05.summary: Two ruling-elder nominees challenged the Session’s refusal to approve them based on their theonomic views and perceived divisiveness. The full SJC denied the complaint, holding that the court of original jurisdiction may assess an unsettled theological position and whether it threatens the church’s peace, purity, or progress; divisiveness was therefore properly considered. The ruling did not decide the merits of theonomy itself, and it left undisturbed Presbytery’s annulment of the Session’s categorical statement that theonomy violated WCF 19.4.
1991-05.standard_of_review_detail: The Session's eligibility judgment was to be sustained absent capricious action or bad faith.

1991-07.title: Complainants v. Potomac Presbytery
1991-07.summary: Complainants challenged Potomac Presbytery's 11/12/91 adjudication denying their complaint over the Timonium Presbyterian Church pastoral dispute, arguing they received too little time, deliberation, and explanation. The SJC held the complaint not sustained: a higher court may not overturn a competent lower court merely because complainants are dissatisfied with the amount of input or time spent, and no constitutional defect was demonstrated. Two earlier complaints were dismissed as not timely filed. The timely 12/11/91 complaint was heard 3/6/92.
1991-07.disposition_detail: Timely complaint not sustained; two related complaints dismissed as untimely
1991-07.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC would not overturn a competent lower court absent a clear constitutional violation or other demonstrated error.

1992-03.title: Richard E. Olson, et al. v. Heritage Presbytery
1992-03.summary: Heritage Presbytery adopted a committee report answering a session's reference on whether a session may require officers to abstain from beverage alcohol. Olson and others complained. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed with the General Assembly, and independently ruled that a court's response to a non-judicial reference seeking advice under BCO 41-3 is not complainable. Complainants may submit their questions to the Committee on Constitutional Business. Confirmed 23-0.
1992-03.disposition_detail: Administratively out of order as untimely; response to a non-judicial reference held not complainable

1992-04.title: William A. Conrad, et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
1992-04.summary: Complainants alleged Central Carolina Presbytery failed to act when it remanded their complaints against the Prosperity Presbyterian Church Session to the commission acting as Interim Session. The SJC held Presbytery did not fail to act: that Interim Session was the court of original jurisdiction and should adjudicate the complaints timely. The SJC judged the complaint administratively out of order and remanded it to the Interim Session, reminding complainants of their right to appeal to a higher court.
1992-04.disposition_detail: Complaint administratively out of order; underlying complaints remanded to the Interim Session for adjudication

1992-05.title: Parks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
1992-05.summary: Complainants challenged a Session plan under which most elders voluntarily resigned, the Session granted severance and benefits to its former pastor, proposed about a year with an interim pastor before a permanent call, and contemplated revising local bylaws. The SJC denied all four items. It held that the BCO permitted jointly considered voluntary resignations, that severance concerned resignation and the budget rather than a pastoral call, and that the plan and bylaw proposal were not themselves unconstitutional. Any later call still had to follow the BCO without undue delay, and local bylaws had to remain consistent with it.

1992-07.title: Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery (Case #2)
1992-07.summary: A complaint arising from Central Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to prosecute TE Stephen O. Stout and to recognize his accusers as voluntary prosecutors was denied. The SJC framed two issues and answered both yes: the Presbytery could constitutionally adopt its Investigative Committee report and decline judicial process, because the Committee found no “strong presumption of guilt” under BCO 31-2; and it could refuse voluntary-prosecutor status, because BCO 31-1/31-3 left discipline to the Presbytery and made any voluntary prosecutor subject to its approval. The complaint was denied on both issues.

1992-08.title: Reference from Central Carolina Presbytery
1992-08.disposition_detail: Reference declined; all referred matters returned to Central Carolina Presbytery
1992-08.summary: Central Carolina Presbytery asked the SJC to adjudicate two complaints and a related reference concerning charges against church members. 2000-07.title: Ed Stadick v. Northern Illinois Presbytery

2000-07.disposition_detail: Found out of order because not timely filed

2002-17.title: Sung K. Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2002-17.summary: TE Sung K. Kim appealed his deposition by Korean Capital Presbytery, but the SJC declared the appeal judicially out of order. Because Kim had not submitted to a regular trial, he was not entitled to appeal under BCO 42-2; the Presbytery had instead found him guilty of contumacy and deposed him from office under BCO 34-4. The ruling disposes of the appeal without reaching its merits and leaves the deposition in force.
2002-17.disposition_detail: Appeal found judicially out of order under BCO 42-2

2008-10.title: Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
2008-10.summary: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s approval of a candidate who believed women could hold the diaconal office but promised to follow the BCO, which permits only men to be ordained as deacons. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed approval of his ordination examination. It held that a BCO difference is evaluated through compliance, doctrinal, and ordination-vow inquiries; the record supported compliance and a credible vow, while complainants had not identified violated doctrinal standards. Absent contrary evidence, Presbytery’s judgment received deference.

2009-01.title: Morton H. Smith v. Western Carolina Presbytery

2009-01.disposition_detail: Answered by reference to the SJC decision in Case 2008-15

2011-16.title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
2011-16.summary: Hahn challenged Presbytery’s refusal to appoint a prosecutor and institute process against Lisa Ridenour, RE Glen Ridenour, and TE Eric Huber. The SJC denied the complaint because Presbytery found BCO 31-8 applicable to Hahn’s accusations and found insufficient evidence of a strong presumption of guilt; the record showed no clear error. A separate concurrence agreed with the result but cautioned against implying that filing charges generally compels process, emphasizing a church court’s broader discretion to investigate and decline prosecution.

2016-10.title: Korean Northwest Presbytery
2016-10.summary: The SJC approved a motion to accept Korean Northwest Presbytery's amended and corrected responses to exceptions on a roll-call vote; Neikirk dissented and Dowling abstained, with three members absent. The amended responses therefore stand accepted. The source supplies no underlying exception content or reasons, so the action is a procedural acceptance rather than a merits ruling.

2018-01.title: Glen Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
2018-01.summary: A ruling elder appealed convictions and censures arising from his brief refusal to leave a closed Temporary Session meeting. The SJC affirmed only his conviction for failing to submit to church government, because he knowingly attended and his apology acknowledged fault; it reversed findings of dereliction, sedition, rioting, and the balance for lack of supporting evidence. It rejected his first four appeal specifications, but held suspension and deposition excessive, substituted Admonition, and restored both sacraments and office, although he belonged to no particular Session.
2018-01.disposition_detail: Appeal sustained in part; censures reversed and replaced with admonition; related complaint moot

It vacated the communications directive and annulled the stay for lack of the required prior citation. It upheld committee examination of the BCO 40-5 reports and did not reach alleged partiality; the Session trials were to proceed.

2023-08.title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
2023-08.summary: Session elders challenged Presbytery’s handling of a withdrawn mediation complaint, document and congregational-notice directives, BCO 40-5 reports, and a stay of Session trials. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main: the mediation complaint was never formally filed and became moot; Presbytery could require official record materials but not compel personal communications or force the Session to address its congregation; and the stay lacked a prior BCO 40-5 citation. It upheld appointing a committee to examine the reports, did not reach alleged partiality, vacated the overbroad directive, annulled the stay, and returned the trials to Session.
2023-08.disposition_detail: Complaints sustained in the main; one specification denied and one not reached

2025-12.title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery
2025-12.summary: Two ministers appealed Presbytery’s divestiture of their offices after their congregations left the PCA. The SJC reversed because their calls had never been formally dissolved, so they were not automatically without call, and BCO 34-10 did not apply while they remained actively engaged and accepted in ministry. The SJC could not judge their fairness and pretext claims from the record. It restored them to good standing and required Presbytery to dissolve the existing calls before pursuing lawful alternatives.
2025-12.disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; divestitures reversed and both ministers restored to good standing
2025-12.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery clearly erred in judgment and acted unconstitutionally under BCO 34-10; it construed BCO 13-2 and 34-10 while declining to resolve disputed factual matters outside the record.

2025-13.title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery
2025-13.summary: Two ministers appealed Presbytery’s decision to divest them of office without censure after their congregations left the PCA. The SJC sustained the BCO-violation specification and reversed the divestitures: their calls had never been formally dissolved, and BCO 34-10 did not apply because they continued performing ministerial functions and remained accepted by their churches. It declined as unable to judge claims that Presbytery disregarded their emails or used the procedure as discriminatory pretext. The ministers returned to good standing; Presbytery must dissolve their existing PCA calls and then pursue a BCO-consistent option.
2025-13.disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; divestitures reversed and both ministers restored to good standing
2025-13.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery clearly erred in judgment and acted unconstitutionally under BCO 34-10; it construed BCO 13-2 and 34-10 while declining to resolve disputed factual matters outside the record.

1980-03.summary: Teaching Elders challenged Calvary Presbytery’s use of the extraordinary clause to examine and ordain a candidate who had completed only one quarter of Hebrew. The Assembly sustained the complaint’s single specification because Presbytery had not demonstrated either extraordinary circumstances or the man’s proven extraordinary gifts. It found the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order and remanded for correction. Rather than answer the broader question about proper use of the clause, it ordered a report to the Ninth General Assembly.
1980-03.disposition_detail: Error sustained; ordination matter remanded to Calvary Presbytery for correction

1981-01.summary: Members of a congregation challenged Grace Presbytery's formation of an administrative commission, its method of appointing the commission, and its refusal to dissolve the pastoral relationship after a 26-16 congregational vote. The General Assembly adopted its Judicial Commission's judgment declining to sustain each item or the complaint as a whole because none of the challenged actions violated the BCO. It also urged all parties to continue efforts toward reconciliation.
1981-01.disposition_detail: Items 1–3 and the complaint as a whole not sustained; no BCO violation found
1981-01.standard_of_review_detail: The complaint expressly challenged presbytery judgment and discretion; no constitutional violation was found.

1982-04.summary: Complainants challenged Grace Presbytery's refusal to ask the Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over allegations against a minister in Western Carolinas Presbytery. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because Western Carolinas had not refused jurisdiction. It nevertheless directed that presbytery to proceed at its next stated meeting and held the one-year limitation inapplicable because its commission had unduly delayed formal process. The ruling was conditional, not an unqualified endorsement of the handling below.
1982-04.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained conditionally; Western Carolinas Presbytery directed to proceed under BCO 32-3 and following

1982-05.summary: The Session challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to rescind its resolution calling voluntary total abstinence from alcohol the proper Christian lifestyle. The General Assembly unanimously sustained the complaint, adopting the commission’s conclusion that the resolution in practice bound consciences and exceeded Scripture’s requirements contrary to the Westminster Confession. The judgment did not expressly rescind the resolution, and it distinguished improper conscience-binding from permissible teaching and counseling against alcohol abuse and intemperance.
1982-05.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; total-abstinence resolution held to bind conscience beyond Scripture
1982-05.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment interpreted the constitutional prohibition against binding conscience by human commands in WCF 20-2.

1983-01.summary: A teaching elder confessed adultery, but Presbytery charged him only with ninth-commandment violations, admonished him, and required him to reconsider his call. The complaint alleged Presbytery failed to take BCO 34-7 action and improperly reduced the charges. The Commission sustained both items and remanded for a new trial, reasoning that the confessed sins were not considered and the censure was not commensurate with the offenses charged; it did not itself convict or sentence him. It adopted a recommendation directing Presbytery to follow BCO disciplinary procedures.
1983-01.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in all parts; case remanded for a new trial under proper BCO procedure
1983-01.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment reviewed the lower court's disciplinary procedure and proportionality against BCO 34-7.

1983-02.summary: The General Assembly sustained a complaint against Ascension Presbytery for sustaining a candidate's ordination trials despite exceptions to PCA constitutional standards. The Commission upheld specifications that his Lord's Supper and baptism views denied required visible-church membership and that his women-deacons view conflicted with the BCO; it rejected specifications on Sabbath recreation and immersion. The Assembly annulled the Presbytery's sustaining action, but not the ordination itself, so the candidate remained on the roll. It directed correction of the trial and pastoral instruction, with possible discipline if his views persisted.
1983-02.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; ordination-trial action annulled, with corrective and pastoral directions; protest recorded
1983-02.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment determined whether stated exceptions conformed to the PCA's constitutional standards.

1983-07.summary: Complainants challenged North Georgia Presbytery’s approval of John Parrish’s transfer examination after he denied that the first day of the week is the Christian Sabbath. The General Assembly sustained the specification of error and annulled Presbytery’s action, characterizing the teaching as a fundamental element of doctrine. Presbytery was directed to instruct Parrish and, only if his view conformed to Scripture, the doctrinal standards, and the BCO, re-examine him in that area.
1983-07.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; action sustaining the transfer-license examination annulled; instruction and re-examination directed
1983-07.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment interpreted the Sabbath doctrine required by the Westminster Confession and Catechisms.

1983-08.summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery’s called meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adopted adjudication sustained the objection to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote because Robert’s Rules required a two-thirds vote, and sustained without stated grounds the objection to ordering the dissolved commission to reassemble and revote. It rejected the challenges to the called meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its consideration of David Alexander’s complaint; the membership claim failed because church membership is not itself a court. No express remedy was ordered.
1983-08.disposition_detail: Items 2 and 3 sustained; Items 1, 4, and 5 not sustained
1983-08.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment primarily resolved procedural and jurisdictional questions.

1983-09.summary: The Session of Village Chapel Presbyterian Church complained that Eastern Carolina Presbytery improperly lifted its matter from the table, alleging refusal of reasonable indulgence, improper evidence, and haste. The Commission adjudged the complaint abandoned: after public notice and a two-day recess, the complainant neither appeared nor sent counsel and gave no satisfactory explanation, as BCO 42-10 requires for complaints. Separately, it confirmed the SCJB's Reference 8 advice—six questions belonged in complaint or review and control; the seventh only required referring the applicant to the BCO.
1983-09.disposition_detail: Complaint abandoned for nonappearance under BCO 42-10; interim advice on Reference 8 confirmed

1983-12.summary: Complainants challenged a called Presbytery meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adjudication sustained objections to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote and ordering the dissolved commission to reconvene and revote. A commission with power could be dismissed only by a two-thirds vote under Robert’s Rules; no separate ground was stated for the reconvening issue. Challenges to the meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its receipt of another complaint were not sustained. No relief was specified.
1983-12.disposition_detail: Items 1–3 sustained; judgment on Item 4 reserved

1983-13.summary: Presbytery members challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery’s denial of Ron Harris’s licensure. The complaint was sustained regarding the improperly adopted supermajority rule and the insufficiency of objections concerning counseling, evangelistic preaching, and sovereign grace; claims that pertinent data was excluded and requests to hear Harris preach were blocked were not sustained. Citing the fragmented examination and sharply differing views, the Assembly urged a complete reexamination at one meeting. It did not order Harris licensed or formally remand the matter.
1983-13.disposition_detail: Specifications 1, 4, 5, and 6 sustained; specifications 2 and 3 not sustained; re-examination urged
1983-13.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment evaluated the presbytery's examination and licensure judgment for procedural and evidentiary error.

1983-15.summary: A presbytery was challenged for allegedly failing to carry out General Assembly directives restoring dismissed New Life congregation members and for allowing the pastor and session to evade compliance; the complainant asked the Committee on Judicial Business to dissolve the pastoral relation and impose censure. The CJB did not sustain the complaint. The supplied record states that disposition but contains no adopted reasoning, findings, or remedial order, so the basis for the ruling cannot be stated.
1983-15.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained as improperly framed; matter treated as a protest, with substance addressed in related cases

1980-02.summary: TE Rod Mays complained that New River Presbytery failed to address reported scandalous conduct by one of its ministers. The judicial commission sustained the specification of error by a 9-8 vote, explaining that required procedures concerning public offenses had not been followed, the responsible presbytery committee had not reported, and the proceedings had not been properly recorded.
1980-02.disposition_detail: Specification of error sustained 9-8; procedural failures identified
1980-02.standard_of_review_detail: The commission identified procedural failures but did not state a distinct standard of review.

1983-14.title: RE Truman Swain et al. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
1983-14.summary: A session's complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery for lifting from the table a matter concerning the church was abandoned because neither the complainant nor counsel appeared before the Commission within two days, despite public notice and a recess, and no satisfactory explanation was given. The Commission also confirmed and adopted the SCJB's interim advice on Reference 8: six questions were properly declined as redressable by complaint or review and control, while the seventh only required referring the applicant to the BCO.
1983-14.disposition_detail: Complaint abandoned; no merits judgment located

1997-12.summary: The SJC record shows that Raymond Larsen’s complaints against Pacific Presbytery—case 97-12, with 97-10—were withdrawn by the complainants. No separate merits opinion was published, and the source supplies no underlying issue, adopted reasoning, issue-level ruling, or relief. The operative disposition is therefore withdrawal, not a merits determination.

1997-14.summary: The SJC deemed Onda George’s complaint against Central Florida Presbytery abandoned because the complainant died without heirs. The sparse record does not identify the challenged action or contain a merits determination.
1997-14.disposition_detail: Abandoned after death of complainant without heirs

1997-15.summary: The SJC deemed Onda George’s complaint against Central Florida Presbytery abandoned because George died without heirs. The short record does not identify the challenged action or provide a merits ruling.
1997-15.disposition_detail: Docket entry recording abandonment after death of complainant without heirs

1998-03.summary: The SJC approved a panel action dismissing Robert Williams's appeal against South Texas Presbytery as administratively out of order. The sparse record does not identify the challenged Presbytery action or explain the administrative defect, so it supports no conclusion about the merits.
1998-03.disposition_detail: Appeal dismissed as administratively out of order

1998-04.title: Jeffrey Yelton v. Westminster Presbytery
1998-04.disposition_detail: No longer in order after the complainant joined another denomination
1998-04.summary: The SJC declared Yelton’s complaint against Westminster Presbytery no longer in order after documentation showed that he had joined the Presbytery of the Alleghenies of the Reformed Presbyterian Church of North America. The brief ruling does not identify the conduct challenged in the complaint or decide its merits.

1998-06.title: Daniel C. Kim v. Korean Southwest Presbytery
1998-06.disposition_detail: No longer in order after the parties withdrew from the PCA to form an independent congregation
1998-06.summary: The SJC did not reach the unidentified action challenged by Daniel C. Kim against Korean Southwest Presbytery. It approved a recommendation that the complaint was no longer in order because Kim and others reportedly withdrew from the PCA to form an independent congregation. Under BCO 43-1, a complainant must be a communing member subject to the respondent court’s jurisdiction; no merits ruling was made.

1998-07.summary: A complainant failed to file a complaint after Korean Capital Presbytery dealt with his case at a called meeting. The SJC therefore approved the Panel’s recommendation declaring the matter administratively out of order. The notice provides no ruling on the underlying dispute and states no further relief or proceedings.
1998-07.disposition_detail: Administratively out of order because no complaint was filed after lower-court action

1999-06.title: Robert M. Shive v. Central Carolina Presbytery
1999-06.disposition_detail: Appeal not sustained; Presbytery did not err on either issue
1999-06.summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s affirmance of his excommunication, contending that SJC Case 97-9 had reversed his four guilty verdicts and precluded increased censure. The SJC did not sustain either issue. Case 97-9 had reversed only the original censure, leaving guilt intact. Because the offender bore the burden of showing repentance, and Session’s contrary factual determination received great deference absent clear error, the later excommunication remained in effect.

2000-03.title: Memorial of South Coast Presbytery
2000-03.summary: The 29th General Assembly record reports that the South Coast Memorial was withdrawn. No separate merits opinion, reason for withdrawal, or ruling on the memorial’s substance was published. The sparse record does not identify a BCO provision or further proceedings.

2000-05.summary: Robert H. King's complaint against Evangel Presbytery was recorded as abandoned. No merits opinion was published, and the sparse record identifies neither the underlying dispute nor a reason for the abandonment. The case therefore supplies only its procedural termination, not a merits determination or relief.

2001-35.title: Moon K. Ham et al. v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-35.summary: A complaint that presented allegations to Presbytery, rather than challenging presbytery action or inaction, was ruled administratively out of order by the Standing Judicial Commission. The SJC did not reach the merits and granted no relief. The source is a short status ruling only.
2001-35.disposition_detail: Allegations not presented in the form of a complaint against presbytery action under BCO 43-1

2001-36.title: Moo S. Lim et al. v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-36.summary: The SJC ruled Moo S. Lim and others’ otherwise-unspecified complaint against Korean Capital Presbytery moot because of decisions in Cases 2000-9 and 2001-8. The brief entry gives no merits ruling, relief, or explanation of those prior decisions. Although the combined catalog header also says “dismissed,” the operative entry for Case 2001-36 states only that it was moot.
2001-36.disposition_detail: Moot in light of related cases; no independent opinion or findings

2007-06.title: Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
2007-06.summary: Lee challenged irregular Presbytery meetings, classification of his interim pastorate as stated supply, expiration of his term, and appointment of a Judicial Commission. Meeting-related concerns were moot or resolved by nullification; the SJC otherwise denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery. No pastoral call had been approved or installation conducted, and BCO 22-6 limited the stated-supply relationship to one year absent renewal. The ruling approved only the Commission’s appointment, not its later actions, which remained subject to pending complaints.
2007-06.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; Korean Eastern Presbytery's decision affirmed
2007-06.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC reviewed presbytery judgment concerning the pastoral relationship with deference.

2007-07.summary: RE Han challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s treatment of TE Lee as stated supply rather than pastor, its clarification of its earlier action, and its appointment of a Pulpit Commission. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery: Lee lacked an approved pastoral call or installation, “interim pastor” meant stated supply under BCO 22, and his unrenewed one-year term had expired. BCO 15-2 permitted the commission’s appointment to process stated-supply requests. The ruling did not approve or disapprove the commission’s later actions.
2007-07.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; appointment and scope of stated-supply commission affirmed under BCO 15-2
2007-07.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted BCO 15-2's authority to appoint commissions.

2008-01.summary: Two consolidated complaints challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s licensing and ordination of a candidate who believed Scripture could permit women to hold the deacon’s office but promised to follow the BCO and not ordain women. The SJC denied both complaints and affirmed Presbytery. It distinguished subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices, applied a three-part inquiry, and deferred to Presbytery on the candidate’s credible vow. Because complainants identified no violated doctrinal standard, no error was shown. The ruling reaffirmed that the BCO bars ordaining women as deacons.
2008-01.disposition_detail: Complaints denied; Philadelphia Presbytery's licensing and ordination decisions affirmed; dissent recorded
2008-01.standard_of_review_detail: Constitutional interpretation was combined with deferential review of presbytery judgment under BCO 39-3.

2011-11.title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
2011-11.summary: Hahn challenged Presbytery’s ruling that CTKPC Session lawfully excluded him from that congregation’s worship until a psychiatric evaluation addressed safety concerns. The SJC denied the complaint. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it found no clear error in the lower courts’ credibility and discretionary judgments, given Session’s familiarity with the people and events. It characterized the restriction as informal pastoral safety guidance, not judicial discipline: it did not bar sacraments, worship elsewhere, or transfer, and attendance could resume upon medical assurance. The conditional local restriction therefore remained undisturbed.
2011-11.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; pastoral restriction and lower-court judgment affirmed
2011-11.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC applied deferential review to the lower court's judgment and found no clear error.

2011-12.title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
2011-12.summary: Hahn appealed Presbytery’s guilty judgment and indefinite suspension from the sacraments, alleging trial irregularities, denial of a requested amendment, haste, and prejudice. The SJC denied the appeal on all three charges: false and unsubstantiated accusations, disobedience and disrespect toward church authorities, and a bitter and malignant spirit. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it deferred to Presbytery’s familiarity with the parties, witnesses, and extensive trial record and found no clear error, even though contrary evidence may have existed. The judgment and censure therefore remained undisturbed.
2011-12.disposition_detail: Appeal denied; disciplinary judgment affirmed because no clear error was shown
2011-12.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC stated that it would not reverse a lower-court judgment absent clear error.

2011-15.title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
2011-15.summary: Hahn challenged Presbytery’s refusal to institute process against three church members he had accused. The SJC denied his complaint because Presbytery found that BCO 31-8 applied to Hahn’s conduct and that the evidence did not create a strong presumption of guilt. Deferring to Presbytery absent clear error, the SJC left its refusal to appoint a prosecutor and commence process undisturbed. A concurrence agreed with the result but disputed the majority’s suggestion that filing charges generally requires process.
2011-15.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; refusal to institute process affirmed; concurring opinion recorded
2011-15.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC treated institution of process as a matter of discretion and judgment reviewable for clear error under BCO 39-3.

1997-09.summary: A church member appealed convictions and excommunication arising from vulgar statements to two patients, challenging the lack of pretrial reconciliation, recusals, the prosecutor’s participation in deliberations, and Presbytery procedure. The SJC left guilt intact and denied a new trial, though it held that a prosecutor may not deliberate as a judge. It reversed excommunication because the record did not show impenitence or contumacy, which could not be inferred from exercising the right to remain silent. It remanded only to impose indefinite suspension from the Sacraments and conditions pending satisfactory evidence of repentance.
1997-09.disposition_detail: Excommunication reversed; remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5
1997-09.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC described deferential review of lower-court factual and discretionary judgments and found the highest censure unsupported by the record.

2000-09.title: Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2000-09.summary: After Korean Capital Presbytery appointed a commission to suspend the functions of Korean Presbyterian Church Washington’s elected Session and replace them without prior congregational consent, TE Sung Keon Kim complained. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery violated Preliminary Principle Six and BCO 16-2, misread BCO 13-9, and impermissibly sought to act for the lower court. Relying on Chappell, it annulled the commission’s subsequent actions as the Session.
2000-09.disposition_detail: Presbytery action and subsequent commission acts annulled for unauthorized replacement of the Session
2000-09.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the BCO and Preliminary Principle Six to define presbytery authority over a local Session.

2001-01.title: Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-01.summary: The SJC addressed whether a presbytery and its administrative/judicial commission could suspend a local session and assume original jurisdiction over charges against a ruling elder. It answered no: original jurisdiction belonged to the session, and a presbytery cannot "act for" a lower court by replacing congregationally elected elders. Preliminary Principle Six, BCO 16-2, and BCO 31-1/33-1 controlled; the commission's interpretation of BCO 13-9 conflicted with those principles. The Presbytery's and Commission's actions, including the censure approved by Presbytery, were reversed.
2001-01.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed; original jurisdiction belonged to the local Session
2001-01.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted constitutional jurisdiction over communicant members and the authority of the local Session.

2001-03.title: Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-03.summary: A minister suspended for five years after a default judgment of heresy and schism appealed to the SJC. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, holding the judicial commission did not follow BCO 32 and 34: no indictment was served, and the record lacked minutes or evidence of a hearing. It remanded to Korean Capital Presbytery for a new trial. The SJC expressly did not reach the merits, the adequacy of the citations, or whether default judgment is proper.
2001-03.disposition_detail: Procedural error sustained; remanded for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34
2001-03.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC reviewed the trial record for procedural error and found the process constitutionally inadequate.

2001-04.summary: A ruling elder appealed Korean Capital Presbytery’s three-year suspension of him from the sacraments. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery’s and its Judicial Commission’s actions because original jurisdiction over a communicant member belonged to his local Session. The ruling rests on the identity of the proper court, not the merits of the charges, and orders no remand or further relief.
2001-04.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed; original jurisdiction belonged to the local Session
2001-04.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over communicant members.

2001-07.title: Andy Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-07.summary: A complaint challenged Presbytery’s suspension of a church Session and installation of a commission to perform Session functions without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled all subsequent commission actions as the Session insofar as the commission was improperly constituted. Presbytery could not suspend elected officers and replace them without prior consent; later recognition could not cure the defect. The SJC also rejected Presbytery’s objection that a related appeal barred the complaint because the cases presented fundamentally different issues.
2001-07.disposition_detail: Both specifications sustained; intervention and subsequent commission acts annulled
2001-07.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted BCO 13-9 in relation to the BCO's protections for local church governance.

2001-09.title: Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-09.summary: On appeal from an excommunication, the SJC held that Korean Capital Presbytery and its special judicial commission were not the proper court of original jurisdiction to adjudicate charges against a communicant member. Because original jurisdiction belonged to the local session, the Presbytery/commission proceedings against the member were unconstitutional and reversed. The ruling turned only on jurisdiction; it did not decide the truth of the schism and contumacy charges. The excommunication therefore could not stand on that record.
2001-09.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-09.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted which court constitutionally held original jurisdiction over the member.

2001-10.summary: A communicant member appealed Presbytery’s findings of guilt and censure of excommunication. The SJC reversed Presbytery’s and its Special Judicial Commission’s actions because original jurisdiction over judicial proceedings against a local church’s communicant member belonged to that church’s Session. The decision was jurisdictional: it neither resolved the underlying charges nor directed a remand or acquittal.
2001-10.disposition_detail: Excommunication and related lower-court action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-10.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over communicant members.

2001-12.title: Peter Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-12.summary: The SJC sustained Deacon Peter Lee’s appeal from Korean Capital Presbytery’s censure and reversed the Presbytery and its special judicial commission for adjudicating charges that belonged to the local Session. Lee, a communicant member, had been suspended from the sacraments for five years after the commission found contumacy and a false statement; Presbytery approved. The SJC held that original jurisdiction over a member’s judicial action or censure rests with the Session, not Presbytery or its commission. The reversal was jurisdictional and did not decide the underlying charges.
2001-12.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-12.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over a communicant member.

2001-14.title: Moon K. Ham v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-14.summary: Ruling Elder Moon K. Ham appealed to the SJC after Korean Capital Presbytery approved a Special Judicial Commission's guilty findings for contumacy, church division/destruction, and a false statement, imposing indefinite suspension from the sacraments (called excommunication in the appeal). The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed Presbytery's and the Commission's actions. Because Ham was a church member, the Session, not Presbytery or its commission, was the proper court of original jurisdiction. The ruling did not remand, acquit, or address the merits.
2001-14.disposition_detail: Excommunication and related lower-court action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-14.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over the member.

2001-19.title: Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2001-19.summary: On appeal from a minister’s deposition in a conflicted Korean Capital Presbytery church, the SJC asked whether the commission followed BCO procedures in instituting and conducting judicial process. It sustained the appeal, holding that no indictment appears to have been served and the record lacked minutes showing a trial, contrary to BCO 32-3’s writing, indictment, and service requirements. The SJC remanded to Presbytery for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34. It expressly did not rule on the adequacy of the citations or the merits.
2001-19.disposition_detail: Procedural error sustained; deposition matter remanded for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34
2001-19.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC reviewed the lower-court record for procedural error and found it constitutionally inadequate.

1997-16.summary: The Session of Bible Presbyterian Church, Concord, complained that Central Carolina Presbytery wrongly accepted its moderator's ruling making RE Chris Dollar's interim Candidates Committee appointment "null and void" because Christ Covenant Session never approved it. The SJC answered both issues no and did not sustain the complaint, leaving Presbytery's action undisturbed. It reasoned that approval was conditional under CCP rules, the moderator expressed Presbytery's intention, Presbytery did not surrender jurisdiction, and BCO 39-3 required deference; it found no appearance of prejudice. Vote 11-7, with dissents urging remand and challenging sessional control over committee eligibility.
1997-16.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained 11–7; two dissents recorded; underlying issue not fully preserved in available record

2002-13.summary: Philadelphia Presbytery was the respondent in a complaint by RE David C. Lachman et al., but the record does not identify the challenged action. The General Assembly found the complaint out of order. No separate merits opinion was published, and the stub supplies no issue-level rulings, reasons, or relief beyond the out-of-order disposition and a cross-reference to 31-35, II, p. 93. It therefore supports only a status note, not a merits synopsis.
2002-13.disposition_detail: Out of order; no unconstitutional proceeding found and BCO 40-5 memorial procedure upheld

2007-04.title: Stephen P. Engel v. Evangel Presbytery
2007-04.summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal to decide his guilt or innocence and its failure to return charges after his Session suspended him from the sacraments without trial or confession. The SJC sustained the complaint on the remand issue: rescission of the censure did not dispose of pending charges, so Presbytery had to rehear the complaint and require the Session either to institute proper process or dismiss them. It declined to determine guilt without a trial record and rejected the claim that the censure’s prescribed form willfully took the Lord’s name in vain.
2007-04.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in part on remand duty; matter returned for proper process or dismissal under BCO 42-9
2007-04.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC deferred on the absence of a trial record but found constitutional error in the failure to remand.

2007-13.summary: On complaint from TE David Kniseley and others, the SJC reviewed Rocky Mountain Presbytery's refusal to forbid a mission church from giving an unordained female staff member the title 'Minister of Church Life.' The SJC denied the complaint.
